title: IBM Defends After 13% Anthropic-Fueled Stock Drop: ‘New AI Tools Emerge Every Week,’ Cobol Modernization Challenges Remain
key_facts: IBM shares fell 13.2% on a Monday, its worst day since October 2000, after Anthropic described new Claude Code abilities for COBOL modernization
IBM replied: "New AI tools emerge every week, including our own"
IBM said translating COBOL is the easy part; the hard part is data architecture, runtime replacement and transaction integrity
Jefferies said the Anthropic threat is less severe than investors perceive
Last week Anthropic's Claude Code security features triggered a sell-off in cybersecurity stocks such as Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike
quote_evidence: "New AI tools emerge every week, including our own," IBM said in a response to a Yahoo Finance post.
IBM stock plummeted 13.2% on Monday, its worst single-day performance since October 2000.
why_it_matters_hint: A reply to an older event: IBM answers an Anthropic announcement.
notes: Older news re-dated: Google News lists CNBC and Bloomberg (23 Feb 2026) and Tom's Hardware (24 Feb 2026) on the same 13% IBM drop; the Stocktwits page itself carries a "Nvidia Q4 Earnings Preview" link and no October date. Reply story: IBM answers an Anthropic announcement; the earlier story is Anthropic's blog post on COBOL modernization with Claude Code (Monday 23 Feb 2026), which sent IBM shares down 13.2%, its worst day since October 2000. We did not carry it in our 3 Oct edition; named here for the reader. Jefferies argued the threat is overstated.
